questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: History: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
questions.text: Which one of the following regions became a part of unified Italy in 1866 ?
questions.solution: Venetia was added to Italy in 1866 (after the Austro-Prussian War). Rome and the Papal States joined in 1870.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: History: The Making of a Global World
questions.text:
Read the following reasons of migration of people from Europe to America till the 19th century and choose the correct option :
I. Poverty and hunger
II. Slaves for sale
III. Wide spread of diseases
IV. Religious conflicts and persecution
options: Only I, II and III are correct.
Only II, III and IV are correct.
Only I, III and IV are correct.
Only I, II and IV are correct.
questions.solution: Until the 19th century, poverty and hunger, widespread diseases and religious conflicts drove many Europeans to America. Slaves were brought to America from Africa; they were not European migrants.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: History: Print Culture and the Modern World
questions.text: The author of 'Book of Marvels' is :
questions.solution: Marco Polo's travel account was published as the 'Book of Marvels'.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text:
Arrange the following categories of forests in India from the largest to the smallest in terms of area and choose the correct option :
I. Reserved
II. Protected
III. Unclassed
questions.solution: Reserved forests make up more than half of India's forest area, protected forests about a third, and unclassed forests the rest.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: 'Sariska Tiger Reserve' is located in which one of the following states ?
questions.solution: Sariska Tiger Reserve is in the Alwar district of Rajasthan.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text:
Match Column I (Dam) with Column II (River) and choose the correct option :
a. Hirakud — i. Chambal
b. Gandhi Sagar — ii. Krishna
c. Nagarjuna Sagar — iii. Kaveri
d. Mettur — iv. Mahanadi
questions.solution: Hirakud is on the Mahanadi, Gandhi Sagar on the Chambal, Nagarjuna Sagar on the Krishna and Mettur on the Kaveri.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Choose the correct option regarding major states involved in the Krishna – Godavari issue :
questions.solution: The Krishna–Godavari water dispute involves Maharashtra, Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Imagine you are travelling from Delhi to Chandigarh to attend a wedding, by road in January. Which of the following crops will you notice prominently in the fields during the journey ?
questions.solution: January is the rabi season, and wheat is the main rabi crop of Haryana and Punjab.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text:
Assertion (A): Minerals are an indispensable part of our lives.
Reason (R): All living things need minerals.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution: Minerals are indispensable because all living things need them, from the food we eat to the materials we use. R explains A.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text:
Match Column I (Minerals) with Column II (Major Mines) and choose the correct option :
a. Iron ore — i. Gaya
b. Mica — ii. Singarauli
c. Bauxite — iii. Chandrapur
d. Coal — iv. Maikala
questions.solution: Iron ore: Chandrapur (Maharashtra); mica: Gaya (Bihar–Jharkhand belt); bauxite: Maikala hills; coal: Singrauli.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Belgium solved its problem of majoritarianism by strengthening which of the following types of government ?
questions.solution: Belgium shared power with regional (state) and community governments, strengthening its federal set-up, so no single community could dominate.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Choose the correctly matched pair from the following (Country – System) :
questions.solution: Spain is a 'holding together' federation. Canada and Australia are federal, and Bolivia is unitary.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text:
Which of the following are the main components of a political party ? Choose the correct option :
I. Leaders
II. Active members
III. Followers
IV. Pressure groups
options: Only I, II and III are correct.
Only II, III and IV are correct.
Only I, III and IV are correct.
Only I, II and IV are correct.
questions.solution: A political party has three components: the leaders, the active members and the followers. Pressure groups are separate organisations.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text:
Study the following table related to 'World Human Development Index' :
India — HDI rank 130
Myanmar — 148
Nepal — 149
Pakistan — 150
Amongst the given countries, which one of the following countries has the highest rank in 'Human Development Index' ?
questions.solution: A smaller rank number is a better (higher) rank. India, ranked 130, is the highest of the four.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: Economics: Sectors of the Indian Economy
questions.text: 'X' lives in a town. He cultivates flowers along with animal husbandry. The work of 'X' will fall under which sector of the economy ?
questions.solution: Growing flowers and animal husbandry use natural resources directly, so they belong to the primary sector, wherever the person lives.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: Economics: Sectors of the Indian Economy
questions.text: The work of which of the following comes in the secondary sector of the economy ?
questions.solution: A basket weaver turns raw material into a manufactured product, which is secondary-sector work. Bee-keeping and fishing are primary; money-lending is tertiary.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text:
Why does it become difficult for farmers in rural areas to take loans from government banks ? Read the following reasons and choose the most appropriate option :
I. Lack of collateral
II. Complicated procedure
III. Higher cost of borrowing
IV. Lack of awareness
options: Only I, II and III are correct.
Only II, III and IV are correct.
Only I, II and IV are correct.
Only I, III and IV are correct.
questions.solution: Banks ask for collateral and lots of documents, and many rural borrowers do not know how to use them. Bank loans are cheaper, so a higher cost of borrowing is not the reason (that is a feature of informal lenders).

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Which of the following groups in urban India depend on informal sources to meet their credit needs ?
options: Both poor households and households with few assets
Both well-off households and households with few assets
questions.solution: In urban areas, poor households and those with few assets get most of their loans from informal sources such as moneylenders, while well-off households mostly use formal sources.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: Economics: Globalisation and the Indian Economy
questions.text:
Statement I: Rapid improvement in technology has been one major factor to stimulate the globalisation process.
Statement II: This has made much faster delivery of goods across long distances possible at lower costs.
options: Both statements I and II are correct and statement II is the correct explanation of statement I.
Both statements I and II are correct, but statement II is not the correct explanation of statement I.
Statement I is correct, but statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect, but statement II is correct.
questions.solution: Better transport technology made faster, cheaper delivery of goods over long distances possible, which is one way technology stimulated globalisation. II explains I.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Explain the role of anti-colonial movement in the rise of 'modern nationalism' in India.
questions.solution: People began to discover their unity in the process of struggling against colonial rule. The shared sense of oppression under colonialism gave different groups a common bond, and leaders such as Mahatma Gandhi forged these groups into movements, creating a feeling of belonging to one nation.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Why did Gandhiji say 'Satyagraha is pure soul-force' ? Explain by giving two arguments.
questions.solution: Satyagraha stressed the power of truth: if the cause is true and the struggle is against injustice, physical force is not needed. A satyagrahi wins the battle through non-violence, by appealing to the conscience of the oppressor and persuading people to see the truth, instead of forcing them; even the oppressor can be won over.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Explain any two problems of the 'global ecology' arising due to indiscriminate use of resources.
questions.solution: Any two: global warming (climate change); depletion of the ozone layer; environmental pollution of air, water and soil; land degradation. These arise because resources have been used without control, for the greed of a few.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: Political Science: Gender, Religion and Caste
questions.text: Suggest any two measures to remove gender inequality.
questions.solution: Any two: reserve seats for women in legislatures and local bodies; enforce equal wages for equal work; promote education of girls; strictly implement laws against dowry, sex-selective abortion and domestic violence; encourage sharing of household work.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: Economics: Globalisation and the Indian Economy
questions.text: How did the process of liberalisation initiated in India in the 1990s, promote globalisation ? Explain.
questions.solution: In 1991 the government removed many barriers on foreign trade and foreign investment. Goods could be imported and exported more easily and foreign companies (MNCs) could set up factories and offices in India, while Indian companies could expand abroad. This increased trade and investment and linked India's economy more closely with the world.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: "Tribal peasants interpreted the message of Mahatma Gandhi and the idea of 'Swaraj' in yet another way." Explain the statement in the context of Non-Cooperation Movement.
questions.solution: In the Gudem Hills of Andhra Pradesh, the colonial government had closed large forest areas, stopping tribal people from grazing cattle and collecting fuelwood and fruit, and forced them into begar (unpaid road work). For them Swaraj meant freedom to use the forests. Led by Alluri Sitarama Raju, who praised Gandhi but believed force was necessary, they began a guerrilla struggle in the early 1920s, attacking police stations.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text:
Story of Rinjha: Rinjha lived with her family in a small village at the outskirts of Diphu in Assam. She enjoys watching her family members clearing, slashing and burning a patch of land for cultivation. She often helps them in irrigating the fields with water running through a bamboo canal from the nearby spring. She loves the surroundings and wants to stay here as long as she can, but this little girl has no idea about the declining fertility of the soil and her family's search for a fresh patch of land in the next season.

What type of farming is Rinjha's family doing ? Describe any two of its characteristics.
questions.solution: Slash and burn (shifting) agriculture, called 'jhumming' in north-east India. Characteristics: a patch of forest is cleared by cutting and burning, and crops are grown using primitive tools such as the dao and digging sticks; when the soil loses its fertility, the farmers move to a new patch; it depends on monsoon rain and natural soil fertility, and gives low production, mainly for the family's own use.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: "That democratic system of government is considered good in which maximum number of citizens are made stakeholders in political power." Explain the statement with suitable arguments.
questions.solution: Sharing power among many groups reduces conflict between social groups, which keeps the political order stable (prudential reason). Democracy means people have a right to be consulted on how they are governed, so the government gains legitimacy (moral reason). Power shared among different organs, levels of government (including local bodies) and social groups lets more citizens take part, which makes the government more accountable and responsive.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Explain the importance of political parties in democracy.
questions.solution: Parties contest elections and put forward policies and programmes for voters to choose from. They play a decisive role in making laws, and they form and run governments. Parties that lose play the role of the opposition and criticise the government. They shape public opinion and give people access to government machinery and welfare schemes. Without parties, representative democracy cannot work.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Why did India adopt the multiparty system ? Explain with suitable arguments.
questions.solution: India is a large country with great social and geographical diversity: many religions, castes, languages and regions. Such diversity is not easily absorbed by two or three parties. A multiparty system lets a variety of interests and opinions get political representation, and parties can form coalitions to govern. It grew out of the nature of Indian society and its history.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: Economics: Sectors of the Indian Economy
questions.text: Explain the difference between public and private sector of Indian economy with example.
questions.solution: Public sector: the government owns most of the assets and provides the services; its main aim is public welfare, not profit. Examples: Indian Railways, post offices. Private sector: assets are owned and services provided by private individuals or companies; the main aim is to earn profit. Examples: Tata Iron and Steel Company, Reliance Industries.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: History: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
questions.text: Analyse the significance of the 'Napoleonic Code' in making the administrative system rational and efficient.
questions.solution: The Civil Code of 1804 did away with privileges based on birth, established equality before the law and secured the right to property. Napoleon simplified administrative divisions, abolished the feudal system and freed peasants from serfdom and manorial dues. In towns, guild restrictions were removed. Transport and communication were improved, and uniform laws, standardised weights and measures and a common currency made it easier for merchants and manufacturers to trade. All this made administration more rational and efficient.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: History: The Rise of Nationalism in Europe
questions.text: How was liberalism allied to national unity in Europe in the early decades of the 19th century ? Analyse.
questions.solution: For the new middle classes, liberalism meant individual freedom and equality before the law, government by consent and a constitution. In the economic sphere it meant freedom of markets and the abolition of state restrictions on the movement of goods and capital. In German lands, 39 states had their own currencies, weights and customs barriers, which hindered trade. In 1834 a customs union (Zollverein) led by Prussia abolished tariff barriers and reduced currencies from over thirty to two, and a railway network was built. This economic nationalism strengthened the wider wish for a unified nation.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: "Manufacturing industries are considered the backbone of the economic development of a country." Justify the statement.
questions.solution: Manufacturing helps modernise agriculture by supplying machines and inputs. It reduces heavy dependence on agriculture by providing jobs in the secondary and tertiary sectors, which helps remove unemployment and poverty. Export of manufactured goods expands trade and brings in foreign exchange. It turns raw materials into goods of higher value, and setting up industries in backward areas helps reduce regional disparities. Countries that turn raw materials into a wide range of finished goods prosper.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: "Agriculture and industries complement each other." Justify the statement.
questions.solution: Agro-based industries such as cotton textiles, jute, sugar and edible oil depend on agriculture for raw materials. In turn, industries supply agriculture with irrigation pumps, fertilisers, insecticides, pesticides, PVC pipes, machines and tools. Industrial development has boosted agricultural productivity and made production more efficient, and agriculture provides a market for industrial goods. So they move hand in hand.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Explain any five bases for assessing the outcomes of democracy.
questions.solution: 1. An accountable, responsive and legitimate government. 2. Economic growth and development. 3. Reduction of inequality and poverty. 4. Accommodation of social diversity. 5. Dignity and freedom of citizens, including women and disadvantaged groups.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Explain any five values of democracy.
questions.solution: Any five, briefly explained: equality (equal rights and votes for all citizens); freedom or liberty (of speech, expression and association); justice (social, economic and political); dignity of the individual; respect for diversity and tolerance; transparency and accountability of government; participation of citizens in decision making; majority rule with protection of minority rights.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: "Recent evidence suggests that overuse of groundwater is becoming a serious threat in many parts of the country." Evaluate the statement in the context of sustainability of development.
questions.solution: Groundwater is renewable only if it is not used faster than rain can replenish it. About one-third of the country is overusing it, especially Punjab, western Uttar Pradesh and parts of central and south India, and water tables are falling. If this continues, future generations will face severe shortages. Sustainable development means meeting present needs without harming the ability of future generations to meet theirs, so groundwater must be conserved through rainwater harvesting, efficient irrigation and limits on extraction.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: "The development goals of different categories of people may differ." Evaluate the statement.
questions.solution: People have different life situations, so they want different things. Landless rural labourers want more days of work and better wages; prosperous farmers want higher support prices; urban unemployed youth want jobs; a girl from a rich urban family may want as much freedom as her brother. Goals can even conflict: an industrialist may want a dam for electricity, while tribal people may lose their land to it. Besides income, people also seek equal treatment, freedom, security and respect.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: History: Print Culture and the Modern World
questions.text:
Print and Censorship: The power of the printed word is most often seen in the way governments seek to regulate and suppress print. The colonial government kept continuous track of all books and newspapers published in India and passed numerous laws to control the press. During the First World War, under the Defence of India Rules, 22 newspapers had to furnish securities. Of these, 18 shut down rather than comply with government orders. The Sedition Committee Report under Rowlatt in 1919 further strengthened controls that led to imposition of penalties on various newspapers. At the outbreak of the Second World War, the Defence of India Act was passed, allowing censoring of reports of war-related topics. All reports about the Quit India movement came under its purview. In August 1942, about 90 newspapers were suppressed.

Explain the meaning of 'censor'.
questions.solution: To censor is to examine books, newspapers, films and so on and suppress or remove the parts considered objectionable, to control what people can read or see.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: History: Print Culture and the Modern World
questions.text:
Print and Censorship: The colonial government kept continuous track of all books and newspapers published in India and passed numerous laws to control the press.

Why did the colonial administration keep an eye on books and newspapers ?
questions.solution: It feared that print would spread nationalist ideas and criticism of its rule, which could unite people against colonial government.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text:
Print and Censorship: The Sedition Committee Report under Rowlatt in 1919 further strengthened controls that led to imposition of penalties on various newspapers.

Why did Gandhiji start a nationwide Satyagraha against the Rowlatt Act ? Explain any two reasons.
questions.solution: The Rowlatt Act of 1919 was hurriedly passed despite the united opposition of the Indian members of the Imperial Legislative Council. It gave the government enormous powers to repress political activities and allowed detention of political prisoners without trial for two years. Gandhiji saw it as unjust and started a non-violent civil disobedience against it.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text:
An Experiment in Brazil: A city called Porto Alegre in Brazil has carried out an extraordinary experiment in combining decentralisation with participative democracy. The city has set up a parallel organisation operating alongside the municipal council, enabling local inhabitants to take real decisions for their city. The nearly 13 lakh people in this city get to participate in making the budget for their own city. The city is divided into many sectors or what we call wards. Each sector has a meeting, like that of the gram sabha, in which anyone living in that area can participate. There are some meetings to discuss issues that affect the entire city. Any citizen of the city can participate in those meetings. The budget of the city is discussed in these meetings. The proposals are put to the municipality that takes a final decision about it.

Explain the meaning of 'participatory democracy'.
questions.solution: A democracy in which citizens take part directly in decision-making (for example in making the city budget), not only by electing representatives.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text:
An Experiment in Brazil: A city called Porto Alegre in Brazil has carried out an extraordinary experiment in combining decentralisation with participative democracy, enabling local inhabitants to take real decisions for their city.

In the context of separation of powers, the given example defines which type of government ?
questions.solution: Local self-government: power shared vertically with a third tier of government (decentralisation).

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text:
An Experiment in Brazil: Each sector has a meeting, like that of the gram sabha, in which anyone living in that area can participate.

Describe the structure of the system in India which is almost similar to the above example of Brazil.
questions.solution: Panchayati Raj. Each village (or group of villages) has a gram panchayat, whose members are elected and which works under the gram sabha, made up of all the village voters. Panchayats of a block form the panchayat samiti, and those of a district form the zila parishad. In towns there are municipalities and municipal corporations. One-third of seats are reserved for women, and elections are held by State Election Commissions.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text:
Loans From Cooperatives: Besides banks, the other major source of cheap credit in rural areas are the cooperative societies (or cooperatives). Members of a cooperative pool their resources for cooperation in certain areas. There are several types of cooperatives possible such as farmers cooperatives, weavers cooperatives, industrial workers cooperatives, etc. Krishak Cooperative functions in a village not very far away from Sonpur. It has 2300 farmers as members. It accepts deposits from its members. With these deposits as collateral, the Cooperative has obtained a large loan from the bank. These funds are used to provide loans to members. Once these loans are repaid, another round of lending can take place. Krishak Cooperative provides loans for the purchase of agricultural implements, loans for cultivation and agricultural trade, fishery loans, loans for construction of houses and for a variety of other expenses.

Cooperative societies come under which source of credit ?
questions.solution: Formal sources of credit.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text:
Loans From Cooperatives: Krishak Cooperative accepts deposits from its members. With these deposits as collateral, the Cooperative has obtained a large loan from the bank. These funds are used to provide loans to members.

Mention any two sources of capital of cooperative societies.
questions.solution: Deposits from members, and loans from banks.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text:
Loans From Cooperatives: Besides banks, the other major source of cheap credit in rural areas are the cooperative societies. Krishak Cooperative provides loans for the purchase of agricultural implements, loans for cultivation and agricultural trade, fishery loans, loans for construction of houses and for a variety of other expenses.

Explain the role of cooperative societies in increasing the income of farmers.
questions.solution: Cooperatives give farmers cheap credit at low interest, for implements, seeds, fertilisers, cultivation and trade, so they can invest in better farming and raise production. Because the loans are cheap, farmers keep more of their earnings and are freed from high-interest moneylenders and the debt trap. Repaid loans are lent again, so more members benefit.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Map skills (text version): (i) Name the place where the session of Indian National Congress was held in 1920. (ii) Name the place where Gandhiji started Dandi March.
questions.solution: (i) Nagpur (the December 1920 session; a special session was also held at Calcutta in September 1920). (ii) Sabarmati Ashram, Ahmedabad (Gujarat).

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Map skills (text version). Attempt any three : (i) Name the leading state in production of Jute. (ii) Name the place where an Atomic Power Plant is located in Gujarat. (iii) Name the place where an Iron and Steel Plant is located in Jharkhand. (iv) Name the place where Sri Guru Ram Das Jee International Airport is located.
questions.solution: (i) West Bengal. (ii) Kakrapar. (iii) Bokaro (or Jamshedpur). (iv) Amritsar (Punjab).
